lessons.title: Use bounded wildcards safely

List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>. Wildcards express the particular flexibility an operation needs instead of pretending all lists accept the same additions. List.of creates an unmodifiable list; our output ArrayList is mutable.

lessons.summary: Change the call to load(true). Which output follows?
explanation: An IOException is checked: code that may throw it must catch it or declare it with throws. RuntimeException subclasses such as IllegalArgumentException are unchecked and do not have that catch-or-declare requirement.

throw creates an abrupt exit toward a matching catch. In this demonstration no real file is read: load deliberately throws an IOException when fail is true. A thrown call supplies no normal return value.
catch(IOException error) handles that type, and getMessage reads its description. Do not catch every exception merely to pretend success; decide what recovery or propagation is appropriate.

after

lessons.title: Close resources with try-with-resources
lessons.summary: Call run(true) instead of run(false), taking the early return after body. What prints next?
explanation: try-with-resources manages AutoCloseable resources. It calls close when the try block exits, including a return or exception. This Trace only logs lifecycle events; real streams release external resources.
AutoCloseable declares close with a possible checked Exception, but Trace overrides it without throwing a checked exception. This example therefore needs no catch for close.

Multiple resources close in reverse initialization order. If the body throws and closing also throws, the body exception remains primary and close failures can be suppressed. Garbage collection is not a substitute for timely resource closure.

body

after

lessons.title: Represent an optional result
lessons.summary: Replace null with an empty String. Which branch runs?
explanation: Optional<String> holds a String or no value. Optional.ofNullable accepts a possibly null reference and produces an empty Optional for null. An empty string is still a present String.

isPresent tests presence; get requires a present value and otherwise throws NoSuchElementException. This explicit guard makes the example safe. Prefer APIs that clearly state whether absence is expected.

Optional.empty is not null and is not automatically an error. Do not use Optional itself as a null reference. Other combinators can transform values later; the present/absent distinction is the core here.

lessons.title: Refine a type with pattern matching
lessons.summary: Pass null instead of "cat". What happens?
explanation: value instanceof String text checks whether value refers to a String and binds a String variable text when the test succeeds. It avoids a separate explicit cast after the test.
With &&, the right operand runs only when the left is true. text is therefore available in text.isEmpty() and in the successful if body. If value is null, this instanceof test is false.
This uses a reference-type pattern, a stable feature. No primitive patterns or preview flags are needed. Pattern matching does not turn unrelated object types into Strings.

Expected output or behavior: 3
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: Prefer a composed collaborator
lessons.summary: Supply new Excited() instead of new Plain(). What changes?
explanation: Composition means one object uses another object to perform part of its work. NoticeService has a Formatter; it is not a kind of Formatter. The constructor receives the collaborator explicitly.

Objects.requireNonNull checks the supplied reference and throws NullPointerException if absent. The final field prevents replacing that reference later, not every possible change inside the collaborator.
A second Formatter implementation can change formatting without subclassing NoticeService. This makes the dependency visible and allows small substitute implementations in tests.

Expected output or behavior: Ready
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
